0.long_answer: Fissured tongue is a benign condition characterized by deep grooves on the surface of the tongue. It is known to occur concurrently with geographic tongue, and its prevalence increases with age, affecting approximately 40% of the population over the age of 40. The condition is generally considered harmless, although some individuals experience a burning sensation or discomfort. The data indicate that fissured tongue is more common in older people and becomes more accentuated as age advances, which distinguishes it from geographic tongue that may present at any age.
